title: Approval gate API & UX: compact audit schema (PRD - WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working PRD sketch proposing a small, consistent API contract and UX pattern for customer-managed networking approval gates + a compact audit log format intended for fast ingestion, search, and forensic replay. Goal is to unify the surface across Private (VPC/on-prem) onboarding, operator-initiated network changes, and customer handoff workflows.

Problem statement (tl;dr):
- Customers and operator teams need clear approval states + short evidence payloads that survive retention and are easy to index when investigating incidents.
- Current proposals scatter attestation, logs, and UI across multiple services making queries (who approved X, why, what was the config) slow and expensive.
- UX for reviewers is inconsistent; many approvals are done in Slack/email which creates unstructured evidence.

Objectives (measurable):
1) Define an Approval Gate API that emits a compact, canonical audit record for every approval decision (goal: < 1KB avg payload).
2) Provide a small review UX pattern (Console + API) that surfaces required evidence, highlights risk signals, and supports fast reversion playbooks.
3) Ensure records are queryable by: customer_id, operator_id, gate_type, resource (vpc/subnet), change_id, and time window.
4) Create a retention + export pattern for customers (S3/NDJSON export) to satisfy compliance.

Primary personas:
- Platform operator (Redwood SRE / Solutions Eng) approving network handoffs.
- Customer infra owner who must consent to inbound changes.
- Security auditor needing immutable evidence and causal chain for a network change.

User journeys (happy path):
1) Operator creates a change bundle (change_id) in Console or API that includes diffs (e.g., route, firewall rule, peering).
2) System presents required evidence checklist (test connectivity snippet, config diff, CFO approval if cost + SLA flag).
3) Operator hits Submit -> creates pending approval record and notifies customer via configured webhook / console notification.
4) Customer reviewer authenticates, inspects compact evidence, and makes Approve / Reject / Request-Changes.
5) Approval event is emitted to audit store and to integrations (Slack webhook, partner syslog).
6) If Approve, automation applies change; system records execution result as child event.

API Contract (sketch - minimal):
- POST /v1/approval_requests
  payload: { change_id, initiator: {id, role}, resource_refs: [...], required_evidence: [...], summary, TTL }
  response: { request_id, status: pending }
- GET /v1/approval_requests/{request_id}
  response: full request + latest_decision
- POST /v1/approval_requests/{request_id}/decisions
  payload: { actor: {id, role}, decision: APPROVE|REJECT|REQUEST_CHANGES, evidence_refs: [...], comment }
  response: { decision_id, status }
- GET /v1/approvals?customer_id=&from=&to=&gate_type=&resource=
  response: list of compact audit-rows (paginated)

Compact Audit Row (single-line canonical record we store/index):
- Design goals: fixed field set for indexing, one free-text comment blob, optional evidence references (URIs), short cryptographic signature meta. Keep size small for fast ES ingestion.
- Example (NDJSON line):
  {"ts":"2025-02-03T14:32:11Z","tenant":"cust_923","change_id":"chg-11a4","gate":"vpc-handoff","requestor":"op_liam","decision":"APPROVE","decision_id":"dec-78f","resource":"vpc-34","risk_score":"low","evidence_refs":["s3://evidence/cust_923/chg-11a4/trace1.ndjson"],"comment":"tested connectivity 10.1.0.0/16->10.2.0.0/16, OK","proof_sig":"sha256:abc123"}
- Note: evidence_refs are optional; content should be minimal. Full artifacts remain in evidence store (S3, object storage).

State machine (approvals):
- PENDING -> APPROVED | REJECTED | TIMED_OUT
- APPROVED -> APPLIED | ROLLED_BACK (applied yields separate execution-audit record)
- REQUEST_CHANGES -> PENDING (after requester updates)

UX sketch (console):
Top-level flow for reviewer:
- Header: change_id, tenant, summary, risk_score (auto), TTL countdown
- Left pane: compact diff (text), connectivity test results, impacted assets (links)
- Right pane: required evidence checklist with green/red icons + upload button (file/S3 link)
- Bottom: Approve | Request changes | Reject + optional structured reason tags (security, cost, outage)
- Each action triggers creation of the compact audit-row and a webhook to configured integrations.

Risk scoring (brief):
- Compute simple heuristic at request creation: num_public_endpoints + change_surface_area + recently_failed_tests + operator_risk_factor. Expose score to reviewer but keep it advisory.

Query & retention patterns:
- Retention default: 1 year in hot index, 7 years in cold archive (NDJSON in customer-owned S3 if requested).
- Query patterns: by change_id (fast), by tenant+window, by operator, by resource. Support exports for legal/cert.

Integration points (notifications & exports):
- Webhook: POST new_decision (compact record) to customer endpoint.
- Syslog/Kafka: optional forward for SIEMs.
- Export: scheduled NDJSON bundle to customer S3 with signed manifest.

Open questions / design tradeoffs (work items):
- Evidence size: do we limit attachments in the approval request and force large artifacts to the evidence store? (recommend: yes, deny in-band > 256KB).
- Crypto: signature model - server-signed hash vs HSM attestation for operator-signed assertions. MVP: server-signed proof_sig to avoid key mgmt.
- Cross-tenant approvals: support for delegated operators approving on behalf of customer (need consent flow and explicit audit fields).
- Long-running approvals: TTL and escalations (auto-escalate to SOC after X hours?).

Security / compliance notes:
- All decisions must be tamper-evident: sign payload, store immutable copy in append-only store, track retention policy per customer contract.
- Role-based access: actor.role must be validated against org RBAC; admin overrides must be explicit with separate audit tag.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- API endpoints implemented (create request, add decision) with doc and examples.
- Compact audit-row persisted to index and exported to S3 on-demand.
- Console review screen implemented with evidence checklist and action buttons.
- Webhook and syslog forwarders available as toggles in tenant config.

Implementation sketch / milestones (quarterly):
- QA1 (2 weeks): API schema doc + small reference server + unit tests (PD-487)
- QA2 (4 weeks): Indexing pipeline (NDJSON ingestion), small Console mock, webhook mock
- QA3 (3 weeks): Integrations (S3 export, syslog), retention policy implementation
- Pilot (2 weeks): 3 customers + 2 internal operator teams, collect feedback

Notes to self / TODO (rough):
- Wire up example NDJSON generator script (liam) -> link to GH PR once created
- Design page: finalize structured reason tags and risk scoring formula (Rhea)
- Security: propose minimal proof_sig format and HSM roadmap (Marco)
- Legal: confirm retention requirements for EU customers (ask legal)

References and anchors:
- Confluence: Private-Deploy-Onboarding (linked above)
- Jira: PD-487 (approval-gate API MVP), PD-512 (console UX)
- Slack thread: #private-deploy-appr-gates (ongoing discussion)

Appendix: sample minimal evidence checklist (rendered as plain text):
- Connectivity test: traceroute (stdout) or test harness URL
- Config diff: minimal patch (unified diff) under 128KB
- Owner attestation: email or signed note (link)
- Security tag: "no-public-ip" or if public, justification

End of working draft — comments welcome.

Unresolved: who is the canonical index owner for cross-tenant search? (ops? infra?). Add to PD architecture forum.
